key_insight: A scaffold-aware foundation model pretrained on small-molecule natural products uses masked prediction and contrastive learning to produce transferable molecular embeddings that substantially improve taxonomy classification, genome mining and virtual screening.
problem_solved: Natural-product chemical space is structurally diverse and sparsely labeled, making it hard to learn representations that generalize across tasks (taxonomy mapping, linking genomes to metabolites, and virtual screening). This work addresses the need for a pretrained, scaffold-sensitive representation for downstream discovery applications.
method: Pretrain a scaffold-aware molecular encoder on a large corpus of small-molecule natural products using tokenization that preserves scaffold/fragment structure.
Optimize joint masked-objective learning (masked atom/fragment prediction) and contrastive learning to cluster scaffold-similar molecules and align related modalities.
Fine-tune and evaluate the pretrained embeddings on taxonomy classification, genome mining (linking biosynthetic gene clusters to metabolites), and virtual screening benchmarks.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners a reusable pretrained molecular representation tailored for natural products, improving performance on low-label tasks and accelerating drug-discovery workflows such as hit finding and genome-guided natural product identification.

paper_title: Pretraining a foundation model for small-molecule natural products
paper_authors: Yuheng Ding, Bo Qiang, Shaoning Li, Yiran Zhou, Jie Yu
